answer: Live video check: before an identity can earn, a randomly assigned reviewer holds a short call and asks for unpredictable actions, such as turning the head or naming the jade or lotus card shown on screen. The reviewer's tool stores only a face embedding hash and rejects any new account matching an existing one, so each extra identity needs a different real person showing up live. Splitting one operator into many accounts fails at the face match. Limit: deepfakes keep improving, a nebula of hired stand-ins can still pose, and storing face hashes raises privacy concerns.
